sophie: Heads-up: sample app upload is occasionally creating duplicate objects in staging. Backend shows two POSTs in quick succession for the same file id. Only seen on emulator.
leo: Emulator only? Device ok?
sophie: Correct. Physical devices never reproduce. Using Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.9.3. We stream the file via RequestBody (from InputStream) to avoid buffering in samples.
nina: Any errors in logs? Stream resets?
sophie: Yes, server log shows first request gets a `RST_STREAM`/HTTP2 `REFUSED_STREAM` or `STREAM_RESET` and then a second POST arrives from the client ~200ms later. No explicit retry stacktrace in app logs.
leo: OkHttp may retry on connection failure / stream reset if the request body is deemed replayable. Streaming InputStream bodies are non-replayable but older patterns could allow retry. What's client config?
sophie: Default builder from sample: `OkHttpClient.Builder().connectTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS).readTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS).build()`
nina: By default `retryOnConnectionFailure` is true. If the client thinks a retry is safe it may resend. Two actions: 1) change sample to use a buffered RequestBody for small files (byte[] or file-backed) so uploads are replayable in a controlled way, 2) document that streaming non-rewindable bodies + retryOnConnectionFailure=true can cause duplicate server-side effects.
leo: Also try setting `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` in the sample app as a quick mitigation for dev/emulator usage. That will prevent automatic retried POSTs but means uploads fail on flaky networks. For onboarding docs we should explain the tradeoff.
sophie: I toggled `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` locally and duplicates stopped. But I'm worried about recommending that globally.
nina: Alternative: detect that the RequestBody is one-shot and add a per-call RetryInterceptor that only retries idempotent methods (GET/HEAD/PUT with idempotency) and never retries POST by default. Add example snippet to the SDK README.
leo: Good idea. Also add a small integration test in the sample app CI that runs against a local test server that injects `RST_STREAM` on first request and asserts client behavior. Catches regressions.
sophie: I'll draft a PR: 1) sample app change to use buffered body for the upload example, 2) add a README blurb about streaming vs buffered uploads and `retryOnConnectionFailure`, 3) add a tiny test harness that simulates an HTTP/2 stream reset.
nina: For maintainers: brief repro steps to include in PR description: 
```
- Pixel 4 emulator API 30 (Android Studio)
- Backend: nginx with http2 enabled, or h2 proxy that sometimes sends REFUSED_STREAM
- Sample app: Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.9.3 streaming RequestBody from InputStream
- Action: upload 5MB file via sample app, repeat until duplicate observed (~1/20 uploads in flaky env)
- Workarounds: set client.retryOnConnectionFailure(false) OR buffer request body (byte[]/File) before sending
```
devex-bot: Issue DEVEX-4370 created: "duplicate POSTs from streaming uploads on emulator with OkHttp" (assigned to sophie)
sophie: Thanks, will include logs and test harness. Also add short note in onboarding: "If you see duplicate uploads on emulator, try disabling automatic retries or use buffered request bodies."
